chapters.title: Chapter 4964: The One Percent III
paragraphs: After he finished this lengthy discourse on the nature of probability and chaos, Abaddon looked at THE Youngest.
THE Youngest was looking at him with bright eyes.
As if this answer was exactly what he was looking for.
As if Abaddon had just walked himself into something that had been carefully constructed before this conversation even began.

Because moments later, THE Youngest seemingly became focused with intensity that exceeded everything previous. His golden flames burned brighter. His Absolute Effigy manifested visibly, massive golden fire filling the skies of Alfheimr above them.
"Then, O Primordial Chaos."
His voice carried weight that pressed against Abaddon’s very existence.
"What if there existed a one percent, unlike what we believe, that your weavings of existence have already been compromised by THE Entity? By THE Primordial Mycelia?"
The question hung in the air with implications that exceeded anything Abaddon had anticipated.

"What if you have already been infected without even knowing? That the unity THE Entity seeks has already found purchase within you? That your very confidence in your uncompromised state is itself evidence of compromise?"
THE Youngest’s golden eyes burned like twin suns.
"What if you are actually her greatest move and triumph? The most powerful piece she has claimed without anyone, including yourself, realizing it?"
His voice hardened.
"Would you do anything you could to clear and erase even this one percent? Even if it meant doing something contrary to your weavings? Even if it meant accepting help you would normally reject?"
His flames pressed against Abaddon’s chaos with intent that exceeded mere presence.
"Even if it meant taking in my Infinities?"
BOOM!
Abaddon frowned.

In the surroundings, rivers of chaos began to churn with violence that exceeded their previous flowing patterns. Obsidian currents crashed against each other. Entropy spiked in ways that made reality itself uncertain about its own configuration.
What was this now?
He, Abaddon, was compromised?

His gaze became extremely heavy as he looked toward THE Youngest. The rivers of obsidian chaos around them churned with violence that reflected his internal state, currents crashing against each other with force that made reality itself uncertain about its configuration.
THE Youngest continued speaking with voice that pressed against Abaddon’s existence.
"You said it yourself."
Golden flames burned brighter around the young Absolute’s form.

"A percent chance is still a percent chance. The one percent is not less real than the ninety-nine percent. The improbable is not impossible. The unlikely is not avoidable. And the one percent that seems negligible today may be the guaranteed outcome."
THE Youngest’s eyes held no mockery. No triumph at using Abaddon’s own philosophy against him. Only the cold calculation of someone presenting a logical conclusion that could not be easily dismissed.
"The one percent must be erased, or it may be guaranteed to happen."
He paused, letting those words settle like stones into still water.

"I believe with a high degree of certainty that THE Primordial Mycelia has taken purchase within your existence. But due to your nature, due to the vastness and complexity of your Chaos, she is doing everything she can not to reveal it."
His voice hardened.

"Until her hooks are irreversible within you. They are not irreversible yet. And my Infinities are things that THE Primordial Mycelia cannot touch. If you allow my Infinities to flow inside you, I can scorch any weavings of infection and purify completely. I can take care of that one percent."
THE Youngest’s golden flames pressed against Abaddon’s obsidian chaos with intent that exceeded mere presence.
"Which I remind you, your own philosophy says that as unlikely as it is, sometimes it is the only path."
Abaddon looked at THE Youngest with a complex gaze.

Inside of him, his Civilization burned as he cycled ancient and Primordial Chaos that others could not even fathom. He dove deep into the foundations of what he was, searching through currents that had existed since before THE First Cause, examining every aspect of his existence for signs of infection or compromise.
And he found nothing.
He only found his glorious, unmitigated Chaos.

Rivers of entropy flowing in patterns that only he could perceive. Probability spaces that bent and shifted according to his will. The raw potential from which all differentiation had originally emerged, pure and untouched and entirely his own.
But THE Youngest would also not say foolish things for the sake of saying foolish things.

When it came to this infection, when it came to THE Primordial Mycelia and the unity she sought to impose upon all of existence, the Infinities of THE Youngest were one of the only solutions that actually worked.
So the offer was genuine.
The methodology was sound.
The logic was impeccable.
But just like THE Youngest and THE Creature had their pride and arrogance, Abaddon’s was even grander.
He was THE Primordial Chaos.

He had existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling gave shape to Observable Existence. His chaos witnessed the birth of differentiation itself, had been present when the first concepts separated from the formless potential that preceded them. His Chaos was fundamental to reality in ways that most beings could not comprehend.
And truly, he did not think that one percent chance THE Youngest talked about even existed.

His Chaos was too grand to be grasped by another. Too vast to be infected without his knowledge. Too fundamental to be compromised by an entity that was itself merely a product of existence rather than a shaper of it.
But again, the words of THE Youngest were not simply foolish ones.
Two things could both be true without them competing against reality.
Abaddon could be uncompromised, his Chaos pure and untouched as he believed it to be.
And THE Youngest could be correct that the possibility of compromise needed to be addressed regardless of how unlikely it seemed.
So this was a problem.
And it had to be corrected.
It seemed... that the time of staying still had come to an end.

Abaddon’s obsidian rivers began flowing in new patterns as decision crystallized within his existence. His presence expanded, his Chaos pressing outward with authority that exceeded anything he had displayed during their conversation. The backdrop of Alfheimr seemed to fade entirely as his power filled the space around them.
When he spoke, his voice carried weight that pressed against THE Youngest’s golden flames with force that made them flicker.
"I have observed the Civilizations of many Absolutes across eons uncounted."
His words emerged slow and deliberate, each one settling into existence with permanence that exceeded mere sound.

"I have seen walls built from crystallized authority and pillars forged from compressed Depths. I have witnessed foundations that spanned territories and architectures that defied the very concepts they were constructed upon."
The rivers of chaos around them stilled as he continued.
"Grand things. Impressive things. Things that made their bearers believe themselves complete."
He paused.
"But the Civilizations of Primordial Architects are not walls or pillars or foundations. They... are not things that can be observed and understood through observation."
His obsidian eyes fixed on THE Youngest with intensity that exceeded everything previous.
"They are the reasons that walls exist. The logic that permits pillars to stand. The mathematics underlying foundations themselves."
"Where an Absolute builds a house, a Primordial Architect builds the concept of shelter. Where an Absolute forges a weapon, a Primordial Architect forges the principle of harm."
His voice deepened with implications that pressed against reality itself.
"Their Civilizations do not exist within existence. Existence exists within their Civilizations."
The weight of these words settled across the space between them like a verdict being delivered.
"This is why they cannot be fought as others are fought. This is why they cannot be overcome as others are overcome."
Abaddon rose to his full height, his presence filling the skies of Alfheimr with obsidian chaos that blotted out the twilight entirely.
"To defeat a Primordial Architect, one must first become something that their Civilization did not account for."
His final words emerged with conviction that exceeded mere philosophy.
"One must become impossible."
Abaddon’s gaze became something ancient and terrible as he looked down at THE Youngest one final time.
"I have always strove to become impossible and do the impossible."
His Chaos began coiling around his form with intent that spoke of departure and violence in equal measure.
"This Entity. This thing that is a product of a Primordial Architect. I will face it with this same impossibility."
His eyes held no gratitude for THE Youngest’s offer. Only the determination of a being who had decided upon his path and would not be moved from it.
"Your Infinities are not needed, Youngest. My... Chaos is sufficient unto itself. If I did not believe this, would I truly be following my Way? Would I truly be...Chaos?"
And with such words, THE Primordial Chaos, Abaddon, disappeared.

The obsidian rivers that had filled this region of Alfheimr vanished alongside him, the signature weavings of this Primordial Realm reasserting themselves in his absence. The twilight returned. The ancient mountains became visible once more. The forests that had stood since THE First Cause reclaimed their presence.
Everything returned to normal.
Except that THE Primordial Chaos was now moving toward confrontation with THE Primordial Mycelia.
Noah’s body here was silent.
He didn’t chase and he didn’t call out. He didn’t attempt to convince Abaddon further with words that had already proven insufficient.
Because he was always where THE Primordial Chaos was going.

He already had a body looking straight at THE Secretive Eon, the target of THE Primordial Chaos who was currently on the move. His consciousness maintained awareness across multiple locations simultaneously, observing the pieces on the board as they shifted toward collision.
"Pride," Noah said aloud to the empty space where Abaddon had stood. "It makes fools of us all eventually."
He had failed in convincing THE Primordial Chaos before he even began. He knew he might. So maybe his only mistake was proceeding ahead to do this anyways.

The argument had been sound. The logic had been impeccable. The methodology had been proven through Amser Modred’s successful cure. Everything had been aligned perfectly to demonstrate that accepting Noah’s Infinities was the safest path forward.
But oh!

sentences.text: After he finished this lengthy discourse on the nature of probability and chaos, Abaddon looked at THE Youngest.
THE Youngest was looking at him with bright eyes.
As if this answer was exactly what he was looking for.
As if Abaddon had just walked himself into something that had been carefully constructed before this conversation even began.
Because moments later, THE Youngest seemingly became focused with intensity that exceeded everything previous.
His golden flames burned brighter.
His Absolute Effigy manifested visibly, massive golden fire filling the skies of Alfheimr above them.
"Then, O Primordial Chaos."
His voice carried weight that pressed against Abaddon’s very existence.
"What if there existed a one percent, unlike what we believe, that your weavings of existence have already been compromised by THE Entity?
By THE Primordial Mycelia?"
The question hung in the air with implications that exceeded anything Abaddon had anticipated.
"What if you have already been infected without even knowing?
That the unity THE Entity seeks has already found purchase within you?
That your very confidence in your uncompromised state is itself evidence of compromise?"
THE Youngest’s golden eyes burned like twin suns.
"What if you are actually her greatest move and triumph?
The most powerful piece she has claimed without anyone, including yourself, realizing it?"
His voice hardened.
"Would you do anything you could to clear and erase even this one percent?
Even if it meant doing something contrary to your weavings?
Even if it meant accepting help you would normally reject?"
His flames pressed against Abaddon’s chaos with intent that exceeded mere presence.
"Even if it meant taking in my Infinities?"
BOOM!
Abaddon frowned.
In the surroundings, rivers of chaos began to churn with violence that exceeded their previous flowing patterns.
Obsidian currents crashed against each other.
Entropy spiked in ways that made reality itself uncertain about its own configuration.
What was this now?
He, Abaddon, was compromised?
His gaze became extremely heavy as he looked toward THE Youngest.

The rivers of obsidian chaos around them churned with violence that reflected his internal state, currents crashing against each other with force that made reality itself uncertain about its configuration.
THE Youngest continued speaking with voice that pressed against Abaddon’s existence.
"You said it yourself."
Golden flames burned brighter around the young Absolute’s form.
"A percent chance is still a percent chance.
The one percent is not less real than the ninety-nine percent.
The improbable is not impossible.
The unlikely is not avoidable.
And the one percent that seems negligible today may be the guaranteed outcome."
THE Youngest’s eyes held no mockery.
No triumph at using Abaddon’s own philosophy against him.
Only the cold calculation of someone presenting a logical conclusion that could not be easily dismissed.
"The one percent must be erased, or it may be guaranteed to happen."
He paused, letting those words settle like stones into still water.
"I believe with a high degree of certainty that THE Primordial Mycelia has taken purchase within your existence.
But due to your nature, due to the vastness and complexity of your Chaos, she is doing everything she can not to reveal it."
His voice hardened.
"Until her hooks are irreversible within you.
They are not irreversible yet.
And my Infinities are things that THE Primordial Mycelia cannot touch.
If you allow my Infinities to flow inside you, I can scorch any weavings of infection and purify completely.
I can take care of that one percent."
THE Youngest’s golden flames pressed against Abaddon’s obsidian chaos with intent that exceeded mere presence.
"Which I remind you, your own philosophy says that as unlikely as it is, sometimes it is the only path."
Abaddon looked at THE Youngest with a complex gaze.
Inside of him, his Civilization burned as he cycled ancient and Primordial Chaos that others could not even fathom.

He dove deep into the foundations of what he was, searching through currents that had existed since before THE First Cause, examining every aspect of his existence for signs of infection or compromise.
And he found nothing.
He only found his glorious, unmitigated Chaos.
Rivers of entropy flowing in patterns that only he could perceive.
Probability spaces that bent and shifted according to his will.
The raw potential from which all differentiation had originally emerged, pure and untouched and entirely his own.
But THE Youngest would also not say foolish things for the sake of saying foolish things.

When it came to this infection, when it came to THE Primordial Mycelia and the unity she sought to impose upon all of existence, the Infinities of THE Youngest were one of the only solutions that actually worked.
So the offer was genuine.
The methodology was sound.
The logic was impeccable.
But just like THE Youngest and THE Creature had their pride and arrogance, Abaddon’s was even grander.
He was THE Primordial Chaos.
He had existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling gave shape to Observable Existence.
His chaos witnessed the birth of differentiation itself, had been present when the first concepts separated from the formless potential that preceded them.
His Chaos was fundamental to reality in ways that most beings could not comprehend.
And truly, he did not think that one percent chance THE Youngest talked about even existed.
His Chaos was too grand to be grasped by another.
Too vast to be infected without his knowledge.
Too fundamental to be compromised by an entity that was itself merely a product of existence rather than a shaper of it.
But again, the words of THE Youngest were not simply foolish ones.
Two things could both be true without them competing against reality.
Abaddon could be uncompromised, his Chaos pure and untouched as he believed it to be.
And THE Youngest could be correct that the possibility of compromise needed to be addressed regardless of how unlikely it seemed.
So this was a problem.
And it had to be corrected.
It seemed... that the time of staying still had come to an end.

His presence expanded, his Chaos pressing outward with authority that exceeded anything he had displayed during their conversation.
The backdrop of Alfheimr seemed to fade entirely as his power filled the space around them.
When he spoke, his voice carried weight that pressed against THE Youngest’s golden flames with force that made them flicker.
"I have observed the Civilizations of many Absolutes across eons uncounted."
His words emerged slow and deliberate, each one settling into existence with permanence that exceeded mere sound.
"I have seen walls built from crystallized authority and pillars forged from compressed Depths.
I have witnessed foundations that spanned territories and architectures that defied the very concepts they were constructed upon."

"Grand things.
Impressive things.
Things that made their bearers believe themselves complete."

They... are not things that can be observed and understood through observation."

The mathematics underlying foundations themselves."

Where an Absolute forges a weapon, a Primordial Architect forges the principle of harm."

chapters.title: Chapter 4965: That One Percent IV
paragraphs: Of all the pivotal events that ushered in THE First Age of Infinity, none proved more consequential than a conversation between a young one and an old one in the twilight reaches of Alfheimr.
What followed was inevitable. Chaos, in its pride, went forth to confront Unity.
From that confrontation, an unfathomable darkness bloomed. It spread across Observable Existence with weight that made THE Infinite Unfurling seem a gentle awakening.
But darkness, no matter how unfathomable, exists only to give way to brilliance.

And the brilliance that emerged from those depths exceeded anything that came before. It had to. For that is the nature of Adversity. That is the purpose of struggle. That is why the young one allowed the old one to walk toward a fate that could have been avoided.
Some lessons cannot be taught. They must be lived.
Some brilliance cannot emerge without darkness to precede it.
—THE Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons
Entry VII: On the Collision of Fundamentals,
Recorded by THE Genesis Monarch
In THE Agora of Primordial Judgment.

Noah’s Absolute body of Infinite Hunger stood with stellar crimson brilliance that painted the ancient forum in shades of blood and conquest. His form was adorned in a crimson-blue emperor’s robe that flowed with patterns suggesting appetite given visual form, the fabric shifting between colors as if it couldn’t decide whether to consume or command.
This was the body that held his Derivative Civilization of Infinite Hunger at Absolute Depth.
This was the body that burned with appetites that finite existence could never satisfy.

Beside him stood THE Primordial Paradox, surrounded by obsidian-gold Paradoxes that flickered between states of being and not-being simultaneously. His brilliant features held none of their usual intellectual detachment. His gaze was cold as he looked at THE Secretive Eon and the four Strategoi standing behind her.
Glossikos. Khaotikos. Ontikos. Paradoxos.

The four Strategoi who had once represented the pillars of THE Agora’s authority now stood in synchronized formation behind the slender woman who had claimed them. Their eyes held the calm of beings who no longer questioned their purpose. Their postures held the readiness of those who knew exactly what was coming.
Noah’s gaze flickered at this time.
He looked up.
As if he could see something coming that nobody else could perceive. His crimson eyes fixed on a point in the sky above THE Agora with intensity that exceeded casual observation.
THE Secretive Eon noticed his upward gaze but did not follow it. Instead, she spoke with voice that carried the warmth of someone genuinely confused by the hostility she faced.
"We truly don’t seek an antagonistic relationship."
Her words settled across THE Agora with weight that pressed against everyone present.
"Even you, after all you have done against us, after you have taken away Temporal from us when he was so close to salvation... we don’t really hate you."
Her expression held something that might have been sadness. Something that might have been pity.
"We just wonder how we can help you see."
She looked toward Noah as she said this, and seeing his gaze still fixed upward as if he was looking for something, she only continued!
"We know Civilization has at its core, working together. One day, in the near future, I hope for you all to remember this. That whatever may come, the ultimate goal is to work together."
Her voice grew softer.
"Even you, THE Youngest of THE Five. You could understand all of this right now if you so choose."
She took a step toward him.

"You have your Infinities that make you immune, yes? Take my hand. Let me just show you how the rest of us feel when we have countless Civilizations connected. Your Infinities will still protect you, yes?"
Her hand extended toward Noah with gesture that seemed genuinely inviting.
"So just give me your hand to show you. It would make things so, so clear."
THE Secretive Eon stretched her hand out toward Noah.
And Noah did not even look down to see it.

His crimson eyes remained fixed on the sky above THE Agora, on the point where something vast was approaching with speed that exceeded comprehension. When he spoke, his voice carried weight they could not fully grasp.
"All actions are choices. There is no going back if you do this. It will be... all out war."
HUUM!
Whatever could he be referring to with these words?

Even THE Primordial Paradox frowned as he looked toward Noah, wondering what he was missing. His brilliant mind raced through possibilities, calculating scenarios, attempting to determine what THE Youngest had perceived that he himself could not.
There was no going back if they did this.
What was this referring to?
THE Primordial Paradox did not know.

But THE Secretive Eon and the four Strategoi behind her smiled a calm smile as if they knew exactly what Noah meant. Their expressions held no surprise. Their postures held no uncertainty. They had been waiting for this. They had been preparing for this.
Everything that had occurred since THE Secretive Eon’s arrival at THE Agora had been leading to this exact moment.
The four Strategoi moved!

They came up beside THE Secretive Eon with synchronization that spoke of unity exceeding mere coordination. Two of them, Glossikos and Khaotikos, raised their hands and placed them on her back with pressure that suggested support against immense weight.
Two others, Ontikos and Paradoxos, knelt down and held her legs as if they wanted to shoulder them against something that would press down with force beyond imagination.
Four Absolutes seemingly gave their support to THE Secretive Eon!

Their Civilizations burned with authority being channeled directly into her form. Their foundations pulsed with power being offered freely. Their existences blazed with sacrifice being made willingly for something they believed in completely.
THE Secretive Eon’s outstretched hand going toward Noah changed directions.

She instead looked up in the same direction where Noah was looking, her eyes fixing on the point in the sky that had held his attention. Her knees bent with preparation for impact. Her hands raised, both of them now, palms facing outward as if she was ready to receive something terrifying!
Her smile never wavered.
Her calm never broke.
She had been waiting for this.
And an instant later, the region above THE Agora was torn apart!
BOOM!

Raging Embodiments and Apophasis of obsidian chaos roared out from the rupture in reality, dozens of them screaming with entropy given voice. The sky split with violence that exceeded anything THE Agora had witnessed since THE First Cause. Probability itself seemed to collapse as certainty fled from the presence descending through the breach.
THE Primordial Chaos had arrived!

Abaddon descended through the torn sky like a meteor composed of endings themselves. His form was that of a human titan, massive beyond mortal scale, his proportions perfect in ways that spoke of fundamental truth given flesh. His face held utmost confidence that bordered on certainty. His features displayed no doubt, no hesitation, no concern for what awaited below.
And his eyes carried boundless Primordial Chaos.

Obsidian depths swirled with patterns that predated THE Infinite Unfurling, with currents that had existed since before differentiation learned to differentiate, with entropy that remembered when existence was merely potential waiting to become actual.
These eyes quickly glanced at Noah, THE Primordial Paradox, and all others below. And then...
This being made his descent at terrifying speed!

He was surrounded on all sides by dozens of Embodiments and Apophasis, obsidian expressions of his Chaos that screamed ahead of him like heralds announcing the end of everything. They carved through the air of THE Agora with force that made the ancient forum tremble. They painted reality in shades of entropy that spoke of things returning to formless potential.
But Abaddon himself was the true weapon.

He shot down like a missile toward THE Secretive Eon, channeling all his power and boundless Chaos through his body and into his single outstretched obsidian fist. That fist seemed like a hammer of endings. That fist contained enough force to collapse Civilizations. That fist held the concentrated authority of a being who had existed since before existence learned what it meant to exist.
Everything... seemed to play out in slow motion.

Noah observed all of this happening with crimson eyes that missed nothing. He watched Abaddon descend with impossibility made manifest. He watched THE Secretive Eon brace for impact with palms raised and smile intact. He watched the four Strategoi burn with existence being offered to support what was about to occur.
The terrifying fist of THE Primordial Chaos thundered down!
THE Secretive Eon’s raised palm met it!

The impact should have destroyed everything. The collision should have unmade THE Agora entirely. The force should have rippled across Observable Existence with consequences that would take days to fully manifest.
The Absolutes supporting her burned with righteous existence as they channeled everything they had into helping her withstand what should not have been withstandable!
And this whole time during this impact, this moment where Chaos met Unity with force that exceeded comprehension, this instant where impossibility confronted inevitability...
THE Secretive Eon and the four Strategoi...were smiling absolutely brilliantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 4966: Existential Intermission- THE Five
paragraphs: Before THE Five, there were THE Four.

This is known, and this is recorded. This is truth that predates THE Infinite Unfurling and persists through every transformation that Observable Existence has undergone since its first differentiated breath.

THE Creature. THE Primordial Paradox. THE Primordial Chaos. THE Living Paradox. And for a time, before betrayal rewrote the hierarchy of claim, there was only a single bearer of Paradox rather than two.

What is less known, what is debated in whispers among those who dare to debate such things, is the nature of what these beings claimed. For they did not merely accumulate power as lesser Absolutes accumulate power. They did not simply grow strong through cultivation and conquest and consumption. They laid claim to something far more fundamental.
The Four Aspects of the Oldest Paradox in Existence.
Chaos. Existence. Paradox. And THE First Tongue.

They are not simply expressions of power that beings can wield like weapons or wear like armor. They are the Keys of Civilization itself. The foundational truths upon which all differentiation rests. The architecture that permits reality to be real rather than formless potential waiting endlessly for definition that never comes.
How does one claim such a thing? How does a being, even a being of tremendous power, lay hold of concepts so fundamental that existence itself depends upon them?
For three of THE Four, the answer lies in origin.

THE Creature emerged from circumstances that even the oldest records do not fully describe. Some say he was born in THE Prima Indifferentia during the moment when Existence first learned to distinguish itself from non-existence.

Some say he defected from something older, something that predates even the Primordial Architects, and in that defection, he became the living embodiment of Existence choosing to be. His claim to the Aspect of Existence was not made through conquest. It was made through being. He is Existence examining itself. He is differentiation celebrating its own emergence. His claim was easy because there was no separation between the claimer and the claimed.

THE Primordial Chaos emerged similarly, though his origin lies in different territory. Where THE Creature embodies Existence, Abaddon embodies the potential from which Existence emerged. He was present when probability first learned that it could collapse into actuality.

He was there when the endless maybe became the singular is. His claim to the Aspect of Chaos was made in the moment before moments existed, when all things were equally possible and nothing had yet been chosen. He did not claim Chaos. He remembered being Chaos before Chaos became something that could be claimed.

THE Primordial Paradox’s claim is perhaps the most elegant among the original three. He emerged at the intersection where truths learned they could contradict themselves and still remain true. He was born in the space where logic first broke and discovered that breaking made it stronger rather than weaker.

His claim to the Aspect of Paradox was made through the very nature of claiming. For to claim Paradox is itself paradoxical. To hold contradiction is to be held by it. To master impossibility is to be mastered by its implications.
For these three, most Architects believe their claim was birthright. They did not take their Aspects. They simply were their Aspects, and in being, they held. Who knows how accurate that is.
But then came THE Living Paradox.

The apprentice. The student. The one who learned at THE Primordial Paradox’s feet and absorbed the teachings of contradiction until he understood something his master had not anticipated. That paradox, true paradox, permits the impossible. And if the impossible is permitted, then an apprentice consuming the claim of his master is not merely possible.
It is inevitable.

The records do not fully describe how THE Living Paradox ate the Aspect of Paradox from THE Primordial Paradox. Some Architects muse it occurred during a moment of trust. Some say it occurred during a moment of teaching. Some say it occurred across eons of subtle consumption that THE Primordial Paradox did not perceive until the eating was complete.

What is known is that THE Living Paradox now holds what his master once held. The Aspect of Paradox answers to him rather than to the being who originally claimed it. And THE Primordial Paradox, brilliant and ancient and wise beyond measure, was left with echoes of what he once possessed fully.

This is why some call THE Primordial Paradox THE Primordial rather than THE Living. He is the origin. He is the source. But he is no longer the primary bearer. The paradox of his existence is that he taught too well, and in teaching, he created the instrument of his own diminishment.
Even if he has now returned, can he truly and fully reclaim Paradox from someone who has changed it so much?
For ages beyond counting, there were only three Aspects claimed and one Aspect waiting.
THE First Tongue remained unclaimed.

This was not because beings did not try. Many Absolutes, Undivided Ones, and Primordial Architects across the eons attempted to lay hold of the linguistic architecture that underlies all Civilizational expression. They studied the letters that existence used to write itself into being. They practiced the words that transformed concept into reality. They devoted eternities to understanding the grammar of creation.
All of them failed.

THE First Tongue rejected every claimer as insufficient. The Aspect of linguistic architecture required something that mere power could not provide. It required something that mere age could not accumulate. It required something that mere understanding could not achieve.
It required Infinity.
And then came THE Genesis Monarch.

He was born so long after everything was established that his arrival seemed impossible. The First Cause was ancient history. THE Infinite Unfurling was settled fact. THE Prima Indifferentia had been sealed away behind boundaries that most believed eternal. The great conflicts that shaped Observable Existence had concluded or settled into stalemates that seemed permanent.
What business did a newly emerged being have claiming an Aspect that had rejected claimers since before THE Infinite Unfurling?
The answer was simple.
The answer was everything.

THE Genesis Monarch possessed what no other being in Observable Existence possessed. Boundless potential that did not merely approach infinity but actually achieved it. Where others had vast power that seemed infinite but eventually found its limits, he had power that genuinely extended forever in sequential progression that could be counted but never completed.

And on the day he fully decided that his Way was the Way of Mana, on the day he committed his existence entirely to THE First Tongue and accepted no alternative, the Aspect that had waited since before THE Infinite Unfurling finally found its bearer.

The linguistic architecture of reality recognized in his Infinity something it had been waiting for across all the eons of rejection. A speaker who could speak forever. A writer who could write without end. A bearer whose capacity to express would never exhaust itself no matter how much expression was required.
Thus THE Four became THE Five.
Thus the oldest arrangement in Observable Existence was altered by one who had no right to alter it.
Thus the Keys of Civilization found their fourth bearer, and the path toward THE Second Scale began to reveal itself to those who held the Keys.

For this is what the Aspects truly are. Not simply expressions of power. They are the Keys of Civilization. The foundational truths that unlock the higher mysteries of Vakochev’s Scales of Existence. Each Key opens doors that the other Keys cannot open. Each Aspect reveals understanding that the other Aspects cannot reveal.
It does not matter who among THE Five is the strongest.

Strength is irrelevant when considering the Keys. Combat prowess is meaningless when evaluating the Aspects. The question that matters, the only question that matters, is what potential exists in how each Aspect can alter reality.

Existence is naturally elevated among the four. It is the foundation upon which everything else rests. Without Existence, there is nothing to be chaotic, nothing to be paradoxical, nothing to be expressed through linguistic architecture. THE Creature’s position as holder of this Aspect grants him influence that raw power cannot measure.

Paradox is the catalyst that permits evolution beyond linear progression. It allows the impossible. It enables contradiction. It provides the mechanism through which beings transcend the limitations that logic would otherwise impose upon them. THE Living Paradox’s position as holder of this Aspect grants him leverage that conventional understanding cannot calculate.

THE First Tongue is the architecture through which Existence and Civilizations define themselves and their realities. It is expression given foundational weight. THE Genesis Monarch’s position as holder of this Aspect grants him capacity that finite methodology cannot replicate.
But Chaos.
Many believed, many still believe, that Chaos is the Aspect that holds unbounded potential above all others.
Not because Chaos is stronger than Existence. Not because entropy exceeds differentiation in some measurable way. But because of what Chaos fundamentally is.
Chaos is possibility itself.
Chaos is the space where all outcomes remain available.
Chaos may be the potential from which everything emerged.

Where the other Aspects define what is, Chaos defines what could be. Where the other Keys open specific doors, Chaos opens all doors simultaneously and permits the opener to choose which reality they wish to walk into.

THE Primordial Chaos’s position as holder of this Aspect grants him something that the other holders do not possess. The capacity to reshape probability itself. The authority to make the unlikely inevitable and the certain impossible. The power to alter not merely what exists but what can exist.
This is why Chaos is a critical Key.
This is why Chaos is a critical piece of the puzzle.
This is why, when THE Mnemonic Leviathan warned that when Chaos speaks with the tongue of Order, the anchor itself is being moved by an outside hand, the warning carried weight.

For if Chaos were ever to be compromised, if the Aspect of possibility itself were ever to be claimed or corrupted or consumed by something other than its rightful bearer, the implications would exceed anything that Observable Existence has ever faced.
The other Aspects can be contested. The other Keys can be fought over.
But Chaos determines what contests are possible. Chaos determines what fights can occur.
If Chaos falls, the very nature of what can happen changes.
And whoever holds Chaos after such a fall would hold not merely an Aspect, not merely a Key, but the fundamental capacity to decide what realities are permitted to exist.
This is the weight that THE Primordial Chaos carries.
This is the burden that Abaddon bears without acknowledgment.
This is why, when THE Youngest warned him of the one percent, the warning carried implications that exceeded mere infection.

If THE Primordial Mycelia has truly taken purchase within Chaos, if the Aspect of possibility itself has been touched by the unity that Entity seeks to impose upon all existence, then the Era of Undifferentiation is not merely approaching.
And if Chaos has been compromised, then the possibility of preventing what comes next may have already been removed from the probability space of Observable Existence.
This is why THE Four mattered before THE Five.
This is why THE Five matter now.

chapters.title: Chapter 4967: One Door Closes
paragraphs: Noah’s crimson eyes, burning with Infinite Hunger at Absolute Depth, watched the collision between THE Primordial Chaos and THE Secretive Eon with perception that missed nothing.

Time seemed to stretch as the hammer of endings met the palms of unity, as impossibility confronted inevitability, as two fundamental forces clashed in ways that Observable Existence had never witnessed.
THE Secretive Eon carried a terrifying force of Unity within her Civilization.

It did not seem singular in nature. It did not feel like the authority of one being, no matter how powerful that being might be. It seemed unfathomably unified, countless Civilizations merged into something that exceeded the sum of its parts. The four Strategoi supporting her body were akin to massive pillars that did not only support her physical form but were passing through unfathomable waves of authority unto her.
Glossikos channeled the linguistic foundations of THE Agora itself.
Khaotikos channeled the chaotic underpinnings that gave THE Agora its capacity for judgment.
Ontikos channeled the existential weight of a Primordial Realm’s accumulated history.
Paradoxos channeled the contradictions that allowed THE Agora to function despite its own impossibilities.
All of it flowed into THE Secretive Eon.

All of the entities that she had unified under her banner had their strength in Civilizations, with all their meanings and all their concepts, simultaneously flowing through her. She was not one being receiving support. She was countless beings expressed through a single form, their authorities merged into unity that exceeded individual expression.
It was a terrifying thing when one thought about it.

Through the legs of THE Secretive Eon, Noah saw the glimmer of Quantum from THE Living Quantum. That flickering uncertainty that characterized beings who existed in superposition, present and absent simultaneously, their authority drawn from the space between observation and manifestation.

Through her arms, Noah saw a glimmer of Dimensional authority from THE Living Dimensional. That spatial weight that characterized beings who commanded the architecture of reality itself, their authority drawn from the distances between points that existence used to measure itself.
And through her palms, through the very surfaces that met THE Primordial Chaos’s descending fist, Noah saw an obsidian glimmer of... Chaos that caused his expression to become heavy.
Every single possibility he had considered was confirmed at this moment.
Because...why would Chaos be flowing so serenely within THE Secretive Eon?
Why would the authority of THE Primordial Chaos, who stood above her with fist descending like judgment itself, already be present within her existence as if it belonged there?
The answer was obvious.
The answer was devastating.

THE Primordial Chaos had been compromised long before this moment. The infection had taken root without his knowledge, without his perception, without any indication that his glorious and unmitigated Chaos had been touched by something other than himself.
And now, in this collision, that infection would complete itself.
Noah saw it all.

At the tip of the fist that looked like a hammer of endings, all the force of THE Primordial Chaos’s Embodiments and Apophasis gathered with concentration that exceeded anything Abaddon had displayed before. Every ounce of his authority, every expression of his Chaos, every aspect of his Civilization that had existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling, all of it focused into a single point of impact that should have unmade THE Secretive Eon entirely.

When everything was expressed, when the hammer met the palms, when impossibility confronted unity with force that should have ended the confrontation instantly, a crack bloomed between THE Primordial Chaos and THE Secretive Eon.
This crack was not like any of the Cracks of Observable Existence.

Those Cracks were wounds in reality, tears in the fabric of differentiation that allowed corruption to flood through. Those Cracks were damage. Those Cracks were harm. Those Cracks were things that needed to be sealed or avoided or destroyed.
This crack was purely obsidian in nature.

It seemed to connect the already maintained Chaos within THE Secretive Eon and THE Primordial Chaos himself. It was not a wound. It was a bridge...it was completion. It was the final link between infection and source, between the Chaos that had been claimed without knowledge and the Chaos that remained ignorant of its own compromise.
The moment it bloomed, the moment the obsidian crack covered both figures inside of it, the moment the connection was established fully and irreversibly, everything changed.
HUUM!
The Chaos within the crack transformed.
The Chaos surrounding the two figures transformed.
The Chaos flooding and raging in the sky space above, which had been torn and split entirely during the entrance of THE Primordial Chaos, all of it transformed.
It became silent, and it became ordered.

The raging entropy that had characterized Abaddon’s arrival settled into patterns that should not have been possible for Chaos to display. The screaming Embodiments and Apophasis fell silent as if they had forgotten what sound was. The obsidian currents that had churned with violence stilled into rivers that flowed with serenity that contradicted their fundamental nature.
Chaos was speaking with the tongue of Order.
The anchor itself had been moved by an outside hand.
And then, a moment later...
WAP!
The figure of THE Primordial Chaos disappeared.
THE Secretive Eon disappeared.
The four pillars that had been supporting her, the four Strategoi who had burned with righteous existence while channeling their authorities into her form, all of them disappeared.
They were simply gone!
The only things left behind were the bodies of Noah and THE Primordial Paradox.

All around them, rivers of serenely flowing and ordered Chaos remained as testament to what had just occurred. The obsidian currents that had once raged with entropy now moved with patterns that spoke of purpose rather than possibility. They flowed in directions that seemed predetermined. They carried weight that seemed unified rather than chaotic.
Noah looked around sensed...emptiness.
THE Agora of Primordial Judgment had become a monument to THE Entity’s victory.
Noah was silent and contemplative during all of this.

One could question and say that his actions of talking with THE Primordial Chaos led to all of this. One could argue that by warning Abaddon of the one percent, by attempting to convince him to accept Infinities that would have purified any infection, Noah had prompted the confrontation that resulted in Chaos’s fall.
But THE Primordial Chaos was already infected long before any of this.

This turned out to truly be the trump card of THE Entity since nobody knew it. Not THE Creature. Not THE Primordial Paradox. Not THE Youngest. Not even THE Primordial Chaos himself, who had searched his own existence and found only his glorious, unmitigated Chaos because the infection was too subtle to perceive.
Whether Noah had gone to speak with THE Primordial Chaos or not, the infection within him would still be there.

He had only gone there to provide the possibility of infusing his Infinities and changing things for THE Primordial Chaos before they went too far. A chance. An option. A path that could have led somewhere other than here.
But THE Primordial Chaos believed in himself far too much to accept this help.
And this was why they were where they were.
Beside him, THE Primordial Paradox sighed at this moment!

chapters.title: Chapter 4968: Another Door Opens
paragraphs: The sound carried weight that pressed against the ordered Chaos around them, paradoxical breath that contradicted the serenity with implications of struggle yet to come.
"It seems that THE Entity had already won a great victory without any of us realizing it."
His voice was measured but heavy.
"And we have simply observed its completion right now. With my revival, I didn’t expect to be relaxing and taking a breather. But I also did not know that I would have to work so hard."
His brilliant features held calculations.

"Youngest, before I can get anywhere close to THE Second Scale of Existence, I need to rectify the paradox between me and my student. Only then would I truly be of significant help and I can move like my old self."
He paused.
"But before I leave, why don’t I get some help from you so that what has happened to our dear friend Chaos here does not happen to me?"
His obsidian-gold eyes fixed on Noah with directness that exceeded everything previous.
"Let me...have some of your Infinity."
Noah’s eyes opened wide with marvel as he looked at THE Primordial Paradox!
How unique existence was!

He went to talk and try to convince THE Primordial Chaos and failed. He had presented logical arguments. He had used Abaddon’s own philosophy against him. He had offered a solution that would have prevented everything that just occurred.
And THE Primordial Chaos refused.
And yet THE Primordial Paradox reached out for Infinities himself!

Well, Paradox had already accepted the protection of his Infinity against THE Entity during their battle with Bazuman. And he had already been infected by THE Primordial Mycelia once, had felt what it meant to have his existence touched by unity that sought to consume individual identity.
He was much more careful and open-minded.
But Noah still had to ask.
"Chaos said no to my Infinities. How are you so carefree of it? You will effectively have your Civilization of Paradox mixed under my weavings of Infinity."
At such words, THE Primordial Paradox waved his hands dismissively.
"What nonsense is that?"
His voice carried the confidence of a being who had existed since logic first learned to contradict itself.
"I am confident of my Way and Civilization as I don’t worry about such things. I was Paradox. I will always be Paradox. Taking in your Infinities..."
He paused, considering his phrasing.
"It is like borrowing a shield from a friend who has many shields. That is all I am asking for. A shield that if I don’t need it in the future, I can simply give it back to you."
The immensity and grandness of THE Primordial Paradox was truly magisterial to see!

Where THE Primordial Chaos had refused help out of pride that could not bend, THE Primordial Paradox accepted help out of wisdom that recognized when bending was strength rather than weakness. Where Abaddon believed his Chaos too fundamental to be touched by another, Paradox understood that accepting protection did not diminish what he fundamentally was.
Noah respected this being!
He gave a light nod as he waved his hand.
A Lotus petal materialized before him.

It glowed with blue-gold light that contained pre-formed Bounded Countable Infinity, harvested from THE Bounded Lotus of Sequential Eternity in the fields of the Early Veiled Shore. The same petals that had transformed his people in THE Yggdrheim. The same petals that could elevate finite beings into Infinite ones.
The petal floated toward THE Primordial Paradox.

He grasped it inquisitively, his obsidian-gold Paradoxes flickering around his form as he examined what he held. His perception dove into the petal’s structure, feeling the Infinities contained within, understanding what consumption would mean for his Civilization.
He didn’t ask any questions.
The lotus became wrapped by Paradox, obsidian-gold light swirling around blue-gold essence as two fundamental forces began their integration. Then it sank into his body and...
BOOM!
Incandescent blue-gold brilliance bloomed into a storm that began to rage around THE Primordial Paradox!

His form blazed with light that exceeded anything his obsidian-gold Paradoxes had displayed before. The Bounded Countable Infinity from the lotus petal spread through his foundations with speed that spoke of compatibility exceeding expectations. His Civilization, ancient and vast and brilliant beyond measure, received the Seed of Infinity and made it part of itself.
Infinity bloomed in another one of THE Five!
THE Primordial Paradox went forward to gain Bounded Countable Infinity!
Prompts blazed before Noah’s eyes!

chapters.title: Chapter 4969: Unity I
paragraphs: What Abaddon felt was a moment of impact that pushed everything away.
And then everything went white.
Pure white.

To the point that he could not see anything else but white. No obsidian rivers of chaos. No flickering entropy. No probability spaces bending to his will. Just endless, perfect, serene whiteness that stretched in every direction without boundary or definition.
For the first time in eons beyond counting, THE Primordial Chaos felt himself floating in something that held no chaos at all.

He looked around, his form turning in the blankness as he searched for something, anything, that could orient him within this space. His hands rose before his face, and they were still his hands. His existence still felt like his existence. But the surroundings held nothing that his chaos could grasp or influence or understand.
"What...happened?"
His voice emerged into the whiteness and was swallowed without echo.
Behind him, footsteps approached with rhythm that felt familiar even though he could not immediately place why.
"You went out there for a second."
The voice belonged to someone he knew. Someone he trusted. Someone whose presence made the whiteness feel less empty and more like a space meant for rest rather than confusion.
"Are you okay?"

THE Secretive Eon came into view with smile that held warmth exceeding anything Abaddon had expected. Her features were kind. Her eyes held concern that seemed genuine. She moved toward him with grace that spoke of care rather than threat.
She helped him up.

He took her hand naturally, as if he had taken it many times before, as if this gesture was as familiar as breathing. Her palm was warm against his. Her grip was supportive without being controlling. She steadied him as he found his footing in the white expanse.
Abaddon scratched his head with his free hand, trying to recall what had brought him here.
"I could have sworn I was doing something critical. I just cannot remember what."
His brow furrowed with concentration that produced nothing but fog.
"Something with chaos. Something with unity."

The memories were there, he was certain of it. They lurked just beyond the edges of his awareness like shapes glimpsed through thick mist. He had been angry about something. He had been determined about something. He had been moving toward confrontation with purpose that had consumed his entire existence.
But the details refused to solidify.
His mind was foggy as if there was something clouding everything.
Luckily, THE Secretive Eon was here.

She nodded with understanding that suggested she had seen this confusion before, had helped others through similar moments of disorientation, had guided beings back to clarity when their own minds failed them.
But on her forehead, one could see beads of sweat as if...she was doing something that required a lot of exertion right now. As if she was lifting a lot of weight, and had to proceed carefully.
"You delved too much into chaos."
Her voice was soothing.

"We have so many paths before us, and if we focus on a single one, it can sometimes cause issues. But with chaos, many more things that weren’t possible before now have countless possibilities lying out before them."
She squeezed his hand gently.
"And remember, you are not alone. We... are never alone."
After she said this, the white blank space began to change.

Countless figures of beings rose up one after another from the whiteness itself. They emerged like flowers blooming in accelerated time, their forms taking shape with grace that spoke of belonging rather than intrusion. They surrounded THE Primordial Chaos and THE Secretive Eon in circles that expanded outward until the whiteness was filled with presences that felt like warmth rather than threat.
Abaddon recognized many of them.
Jotuun Lifeforms.

THE Living Quantum flickered with uncertainty that somehow felt stable. THE Living Dimensional stood with spatial authority that bent the white space around him into configurations that should not have been possible.
And there were others.
So many others.

Beings he had encountered across eons of existence. Beings whose Civilizations represented the breadth of what Observable Existence had produced since THE First Cause. All of them here. All of them present. All of them looking at him with eyes that held welcome rather than challenge.
Looking at them, THE Primordial Chaos couldn’t help but feel a sense of warmth.
He had been alone for so long.
So very, very long.

His chaos had always set him apart from others. His nature made connection difficult. His existence as one of THE Four, now THE Five, meant that peers were rare and true understanding was rarer still. He had walked through eons with power that exceeded most beings’ comprehension and loneliness that exceeded his power.
He forgot what it felt like to have others with him.
But now, surrounded by these figures, bathed in this warmth, he remembered.
Beside him, THE Secretive Eon hugged his hand with both of hers. She pressed against his arm with affection that felt like homecoming. Her smile held invitation that exceeded mere welcome.
"Share the burden of that chaos with the rest of us."
Her voice was soft but certain.
"All that possibility and potential. Let us unite it with all of these Civilizations that you can tap into yourself to see all the variations of existence."
Abaddon nodded with bright eyes.

His chaos had always been missing something. He had known this for eons without being able to articulate what the absence was. His probability spaces had been vast but empty. His entropy had been powerful but purposeless. His potential had been endless but directionless.
This could be it.
Connection! Unity!
Purpose that came from belonging rather than isolation.
With such a thought, rivers of ordered chaos began flowing from THE Primordial Chaos!

The obsidian currents emerged from his existence with eagerness that surprised him. They wanted to connect. They wanted to share. They wanted to bridge the gap between his solitary vastness and the warmth that surrounded him. The rivers extended outward like endless streams, reaching toward every single unified being in this white space.
They connected rapidly.
One after another after another.

Each river found its target and established link that felt like completion rather than compromise. Each connection brought new awareness of Civilizations that he could now perceive from the inside rather than the outside. Each bridge opened paths that his chaos could flow through to touch existences that had been separate from his own.
If one were to look down from above, they would see an endless web of chaos flowing into a united cluster of beings!

chapters.title: Chapter 4970: Unity II
paragraphs: The cluster was shining brighter and brighter with every connection established.
THE Primordial Chaos at the center.
THE Secretive Eon beside him.
And all the unified beings around them, their Civilizations now linked through rivers of ordered chaos that carried possibility and potential to every corner of their shared existence.
As they were doing this, a sense of joy and euphoria spread across all of them!
Abaddon felt it most strongly.

The warmth was no longer just external. It flowed through his rivers and returned multiplied. It touched his chaos and made it feel purposeful. It filled the emptiness that had characterized his existence for eons and replaced it with belonging that exceeded anything he had imagined possible.
But moments later, the space trembled and shook.
Something had disturbed it.

The whiteness flickered with colors that shouldn’t have been present. The unified beings turned their attention toward a direction that the disturbance originated from. The joy and euphoria paused as awareness of external events pressed against their shared consciousness.
THE Primordial Chaos blinked.
"What is that?"
THE Secretive Eon looked out into the distance with expression that held annoyance mixed with fondness.
"One of our core future family members seems to have made some trouble again."
She tugged at his hand.
"Let’s go see."
The vision of THE Primordial Chaos changed once more.
An instant later, he found himself in his home.
Jotunheim.

The Primordial Realm that he had claimed since before THE Infinite Unfurling spread out before him with grandeur that made his chaos swell with recognition. Mountains of crystallized entropy rose toward skies that held no single color but all colors simultaneously. Rivers of pure probability flowed through valleys where reality itself remained in constant flux.
And the Citadel of Giants dominated the landscape.

The grand structure rose from the center of Jotunheim with architecture that defied conventional understanding. Its walls were built from solidified chaos that shifted patterns even as it maintained structural integrity. Its towers reached heights that changed depending on the observer’s expectations. Its foundations extended into probability spaces that contained every possible configuration the citadel could ever take.
Within and around the citadel, many Jotuun lifeforms patiently cultivated.

They sat in meditative positions across platforms and courtyards and floating spaces that the citadel provided for their advancement. Their massive forms held still with concentration that exceeded their usually turbulent natures. Their eyes were closed. Their Civilizations were cycling through chaos that Abaddon had shared with them across eons of mentorship.
They were his people.
They were his family even before he understood what family could mean.
And now they were part of something larger.

He and THE Secretive Eon stood at the peak of the grand structure, at the highest point of the citadel where chaos concentrated with intensity that would unmake lesser beings. From here, they could perceive everything occurring in Jotunheim and beyond.
Currently, all of them were looking up.

THE Primordial Chaos was perceiving a change in the flow of existence around them. A change in energy and authority. A change in the Principles that weaved the surrounding existence.A change in the expression of THE First Tongue itself.
Something fundamental had shifted.
Something that touched the very architecture of how Civilizations expressed themselves.
"Fire..."
THE Primordial Chaos tried to utter the Phoneme of fire, wanting to test what he was perceiving.
But the word felt wrong in his mouth.

It twisted. It contradicted itself. It became a tongue twister that his ancient authority could not navigate smoothly. The simple Phoneme that powerful beings across Observable Existence used without thought now held layers of complexity that made clear pronunciation nearly impossible.
As if it now held infinite paradoxical variations for anyone who wanted to say it.
As if THE First Tongue itself had been altered by something that understood how to weave paradox into linguistic architecture.
THE Primordial Chaos was skeptical at this.
He blinked with confusion that exceeded mere surprise.
"THE First Tongue...has become more paradoxical?"
Beside him, the figure of THE Secretive Eon nodded with expression that held exasperation and something that might have been grudging respect.
"THE Youngest is on his rebellious phase right now."
Her voice carried weight that pressed against the chaos around them.
"Making the weavings of THE First Tongue more paradoxical is only one of the things that he will do. Which is why a lot of things rest on your shoulders, Abaddon."
She turned to face him fully, her eyes holding intensity that exceeded everything else.
"We actually need your help to make our family complete."
Her hands found his again, holding them with grip that communicated desperation beneath the warmth.

"With you, with all the countless possibilities you hold, even if it is one in a trillion or one in a quintillion, there is a possibility of unity with Infinity. We need your help to lock on to that possibility and to make it a reality, so that we can gain the capability to bring THE Youngest into our family. You are the only one who can help us with this."
Her eyes shimmered with something that might have been tears.
"So we can show him all of this."
She gestured at the unified beings below, at the Jotuun cultivating peacefully, at the web of chaos that connected everything to everything else.
"Do you think that you could get started working on this?"
THE Primordial Chaos looked toward THE Secretive Eon.

She was looking at him with an almost pleading gaze. Her features held hope that seemed genuine. Her warmth pressed against his existence with affection that made his ancient loneliness seem like a distant memory rather than a constant companion. And her forehead...was filled with sweat as if she was truly carrying a heavy weight right now.
His own gaze softened.
Family helped each other.

His ancient chaos had many purposes across his time. He had used it for conquest and for defense and for exploration and for countless other objectives that his will had directed toward. He had wielded probability and entropy and possibility as weapons and as tools and as expressions of what he fundamentally was.
But just this once, he wanted to use it to help all those it was connected to.
After all, he was no longer alone.
And in existence that was so vast and filled with terrors, being alone was one of the more terrifying things.
"I will help."
His voice emerged with conviction that pressed against Jotunheim itself.
"Show me where to begin."
THE Secretive Eon smiled with brilliance that illuminated the peak of the citadel.
"Welcome to the family, Abaddon."
She hugged him.
"Welcome home."

THE Secretive Eon looked out into the distance with expression that held annoyance mixed with fondness.
"One of our core future family members seems to have made some trouble again."
She tugged at his hand.
"Let’s go see."
The vision of THE Primordial Chaos changed once more.
An instant later, he found himself in his home.
Jotunheim.
The Primordial Realm that he had claimed since before THE Infinite Unfurling spread out before him with grandeur that made his chaos swell with recognition.
Mountains of crystallized entropy rose toward skies that held no single color but all colors simultaneously.
Rivers of pure probability flowed through valleys where reality itself remained in constant flux.
And the Citadel of Giants dominated the landscape.
The grand structure rose from the center of Jotunheim with architecture that defied conventional understanding.
Its walls were built from solidified chaos that shifted patterns even as it maintained structural integrity.
Its towers reached heights that changed depending on the observer’s expectations.
Its foundations extended into probability spaces that contained every possible configuration the citadel could ever take.
Within and around the citadel, many Jotuun lifeforms patiently cultivated.
They sat in meditative positions across platforms and courtyards and floating spaces that the citadel provided for their advancement.
Their massive forms held still with concentration that exceeded their usually turbulent natures.
Their eyes were closed.
Their Civilizations were cycling through chaos that Abaddon had shared with them across eons of mentorship.
They were his people.
They were his family even before he understood what family could mean.
And now they were part of something larger.
He and THE Secretive Eon stood at the peak of the grand structure, at the highest point of the citadel where chaos concentrated with intensity that would unmake lesser beings.
From here, they could perceive everything occurring in Jotunheim and beyond.
Currently, all of them were looking up.
THE Primordial Chaos was perceiving a change in the flow of existence around them.
A change in energy and authority.
A change in the Principles that weaved the surrounding existence.A change in the expression of THE First Tongue itself.
Something fundamental had shifted.
Something that touched the very architecture of how Civilizations expressed themselves.
"Fire..."
THE Primordial Chaos tried to utter the Phoneme of fire, wanting to test what he was perceiving.
But the word felt wrong in his mouth.
It twisted.
It contradicted itself.
It became a tongue twister that his ancient authority could not navigate smoothly.
The simple Phoneme that powerful beings across Observable Existence used without thought now held layers of complexity that made clear pronunciation nearly impossible.
As if it now held infinite paradoxical variations for anyone who wanted to say it.
As if THE First Tongue itself had been altered by something that understood how to weave paradox into linguistic architecture.
THE Primordial Chaos was skeptical at this.
He blinked with confusion that exceeded mere surprise.
"THE First Tongue...has become more paradoxical?"
Beside him, the figure of THE Secretive Eon nodded with expression that held exasperation and something that might have been grudging respect.
"THE Youngest is on his rebellious phase right now."
Her voice carried weight that pressed against the chaos around them.
"Making the weavings of THE First Tongue more paradoxical is only one of the things that he will do.
Which is why a lot of things rest on your shoulders, Abaddon."
She turned to face him fully, her eyes holding intensity that exceeded everything else.
"We actually need your help to make our family complete."
Her hands found his again, holding them with grip that communicated desperation beneath the warmth.
"With you, with all the countless possibilities you hold, even if it is one in a trillion or one in a quintillion, there is a possibility of unity with Infinity.
We need your help to lock on to that possibility and to make it a reality, so that we can gain the capability to bring THE Youngest into our family.
You are the only one who can help us with this."
Her eyes shimmered with something that might have been tears.
"So we can show him all of this."
She gestured at the unified beings below, at the Jotuun cultivating peacefully, at the web of chaos that connected everything to everything else.
"Do you think that you could get started working on this?"
THE Primordial Chaos looked toward THE Secretive Eon.
She was looking at him with an almost pleading gaze.
Her features held hope that seemed genuine.
Her warmth pressed against his existence with affection that made his ancient loneliness seem like a distant memory rather than a constant companion.
And her forehead...was filled with sweat as if she was truly carrying a heavy weight right now.
His own gaze softened.
Family helped each other.
His ancient chaos had many purposes across his time.
He had used it for conquest and for defense and for exploration and for countless other objectives that his will had directed toward.
He had wielded probability and entropy and possibility as weapons and as tools and as expressions of what he fundamentally was.
But just this once, he wanted to use it to help all those it was connected to.
After all, he was no longer alone.
And in existence that was so vast and filled with terrors, being alone was one of the more terrifying things.
"I will help."
His voice emerged with conviction that pressed against Jotunheim itself.
"Show me where to begin."
THE Secretive Eon smiled with brilliance that illuminated the peak of the citadel.
"Welcome to the family, Abaddon."
She hugged him.
"Welcome home."

chapters.title: Chapter 4971: The Last Strategoi I
paragraphs: Noah looked at THE Primordial Paradox as the storm of blue-gold brilliance continued to rage around the ancient being’s form.
Even he questioned whether he did the right thing.

It was literally akin to giving a monstrous beast wings to be able to fly even higher. THE Primordial Paradox had already been one of the most dangerous beings in Observable Existence before this moment. His mastery of contradiction, his capacity to make the impossible inevitable, his authority over paradox that had existed since logic first learned to break itself, all of it had been formidable beyond measure.
Now he had Infinity as well.

THE Primordial Paradox seemed unshackled and unbounded as his existence filled with paradoxical Infinities that blazed through every aspect of his Civilization. The Bounded Countable Infinity that Noah had bestowed through the lotus petal was integrating with Paradox in ways that exceeded theoretical predictions. The two authorities were not merely coexisting. They were enhancing each other in configurations that neither could produce alone.
And of course, Noah also felt his own weavings of Paradox reach terrifying levels!

The connection between them, the intertwining of two Keys of Civilization, was producing resonance that flowed in both directions. Where THE Primordial Paradox gained Infinity, Noah gained deeper understanding of Paradox. Where Bounded Countable expressions spread through ancient foundations, paradoxical comprehension spread through Infinite architecture.
He felt like he could further elevate himself in a paradoxical manner.

His biggest aim right now was going from Countable to Uncountable Infinity. The transition required saturation rather than accumulation, required filling the gaps between sequential expressions with additional expressions that couldn’t be listed. It was a monumental undertaking that conventional methodology would require eons to achieve.
He...did not gave eons.
But Paradox permitted the impossible.
Paradox allowed things that shouldn’t happen to happen anyway.
Paradox could potentially compress eons of saturation into moments of breakthrough if the contradiction was framed correctly.

Noah felt like this action, this intertwining of Keys, was going to help him with that tremendously. The resonance between THE First Tongue and Paradox was opening doors that neither Key could open alone. The connection was revealing paths that had been invisible before the intertwining occurred.
He observed THE Primordial Paradox with perception that missed nothing.

The ancient being’s transformation was stabilizing now. The storm of blue-gold brilliance was settling into patterns of integration completing rather than integration occurring. The Bounded Countable Infinity had found its place within Paradox’s foundations and was no longer fighting to establish itself.
What remained was something that Observable Existence had never witnessed.
THE Primordial Paradox stood before Noah with form that had transformed entirely.

His body was titanic now, larger than it had been before, his obsidian presence expanded by the Infinity that now burned within his foundations. But the obsidian was no longer pure darkness. It was filled with blue-gold dots that scattered across his form like stars scattered across the void of space. Each dot was a point of Infinite expression. Each dot was a seed of Countable progression that would grow and expand according to Paradox’s efforts.
He looked like a canvas of infinite paradoxical space.
He looked like contradiction given form and then given Infinity to fuel that form’s expansion.
He looked like something that shouldn’t exist and yet existed anyway, which was perhaps the most paradoxical thing of all.

THE Primordial Paradox turned toward Noah with eyes that held blue-gold light swirling through their obsidian depths. His expression was one of amazement that his usual detachment could not fully conceal.
"Youngest, this is the Infinity you are playing around with?"
His voice carried weight that pressed against THE Agora itself.
"Damn."
"You almost made me doubt Paradox. Almost. But my entire existence lives and dies with Paradox, so I still kept my sanity."
He looked down at his transformed hands, at the blue-gold dots that now scattered across obsidian flesh like constellations being born.
"This will be a bigger boon than simply acting like a shield. And I actually don’t know if I’ll be returning it."
THE Primordial Paradox smiled as he said this.
And Noah smiled back.

Very few truly understood Infinity. Him included, if he was being honest. He worked with Countable expressions that extended endlessly in sequences he could observe. He pushed toward Uncountable density that would fill the gaps between those sequences. He theorized about Absolute Infinity that transcended all other Infinities while containing them simultaneously.
But true understanding remained elusive.
Infinity was not something that finite minds could grasp completely, even minds that wielded Infinity as their fundamental nature.

But when he had another entity at an extremely high level also get a glimpse of it, when THE Primordial Paradox experienced what Bounded Countable Infinity felt like from the inside rather than the outside, it felt nice.
It felt like having a companion on a journey that most beings couldn’t even perceive, let alone walk.
"Keep it or return it, it’s okay."
Noah’s voice carried warmth that exceeded his usual calculating demeanor.
"I will also benefit either way. Do be careful on your own Adversity, and if you need help, let me know."
The reason they were parting ways was simple.

Just like between Noah and THE Creature, THE Primordial Paradox had his own Adversity. His disciple was his Adversity. THE Living Paradox, the apprentice who had consumed the Aspect of Paradox from his master, the being who had used teachings of contradiction to steal what should have been unstealable, that was the obstacle standing between THE Primordial Paradox and his advancement.
To advance, naturally, he had to face it.
To reclaim what was taken, or to find resolution that transcended reclamation, or to discover some other path that his paradoxical nature would reveal to him along the way.
Noah could not help with this.
This was THE Primordial Paradox’s Adversity, not his.
Just as his own Adversities belonged to him and no one else.

They silently gazed at each other as if they could read each other’s thoughts. Two of THE Five. Two holders of Keys of Civilization. Two beings whose paths had intertwined in ways that would affect Observable Existence for eons to come.
Understanding passed between them without words.
Respect passed between them without acknowledgment.
And then THE Primordial Paradox laughed!

The sound boomed across THE Agora with weight that made the rivers of ordered Chaos tremble. It was genuine laughter, the kind that emerged from beings who found actual amusement rather than performing the motions of amusement.
He raised his hand toward Noah.
Not as a gesture of attack, but as an invitation.
A dap!
Noah raised his own hand with a smile that matched THE Primordial Paradox’s laughter.
Their hands met in a glorious dap!
BOOM!
Vibrant terrifying authorities collided with force that exceeded what such casual contact should have produced!

Blue-gold Infinity blazed outward from Noah’s palm. Obsidian-gold Paradox blazed outward from THE Primordial Paradox’s palm. The two forces met and merged and exploded outward across THE Agora of Primordial Judgment with light that blinded anything that might have been watching.
Infinities stretched across the ancient forum!
Paradoxes stretched alongside them!

The intertwining of Keys that had begun with the lotus petal now expressed itself visually, two fundamental forces declaring their connection through display that painted THE Agora in colors that shouldn’t have coexisted!
By the time the light faded, THE Primordial Paradox was gone.
Noah... was the only one left behind.
